haiku-low.q1: Held 10 minutes, all-or-nothing across lines. If unclaimed, Inventory's periodic sweep returns the stock to available counts. Order is not told.
haiku-low.q2: Stock is reserved before the charge. If any line is short, nothing is reserved, no payment is taken, status is OUT_OF_STOCK, and the cart is untouched.
haiku-low.q3: The order id is sent to the provider as the idempotency key, so a retried charge cannot create a second charge.
haiku-low.q4: Claim fails, so Order requests a full refund keyed by order id, sets CANCELLED_OUT_OF_STOCK, and emails the customer. Money returns when the provider succeeds.
haiku-low.q5: Cart empties when it consumes the OrderConfirmed event after a successful claim. If checkout fails, the cart is untouched.
haiku-low.q6: Order runs the checkout and moves it between steps. Its DB stores each order, its line and price snapshot, and its status.
haiku-low.q7: Provider webhook reaches Payment, which checks the signature and publishes PaymentSucceeded or PaymentDeclined, which Order consumes. Status lookup fallback is unconfirmed.
haiku-low.q8: Payment stores processed webhook ids and ignores repeats. Order also acts only on orders in AWAITING_PAYMENT, so repeats on finished orders are ignored.
haiku-low.q9: Order tells Inventory to release the reservation after the PaymentDeclined event. Inventory marks it RELEASED and raises the available counts.
haiku-low.q10: Order asks Inventory to claim. Inventory claims if the hold is live or lapsed but unswept, or if stock is still free. Otherwise the claim fails and refund follows.
haiku-low.q11: Payment saves the refund row as PENDING first, then retries the provider until success, alerting after repeated failures. The refund row is in Payment's DB.
haiku-low.q12: The Cart service empties the cart when it consumes the OrderConfirmed event, published by Order after a successful claim.

sonnet.q1: Held 10 minutes. If unclaimed, the periodic sweep in Inventory returns lapsed unclaimed reservations to stock (raises counts). Order isn't told. A lapsed but unswept hold can still be claimed; if swept, a claim succeeds only if stock is still available.
sonnet.q2: Reserved before charging (step 2, then step 3 charge). If any line is short, nothing is reserved (all-or-nothing), no payment is made, order status is OUT_OF_STOCK, customer sees the short items, cart untouched.
sonnet.q3: The order id is sent to the provider as the idempotency key, so a repeated charge call doesn't double charge.
sonnet.q4: Order asks Payment for a full refund (safe to repeat), sets the order to CANCELLED_OUT_OF_STOCK, and emails the customer that the refund is on its way. Money follows when the provider refunds.
sonnet.q5: The cart is emptied only after the order is CONFIRMED (Cart consumes OrderConfirmed). On any failure (out of stock, declined, cancelled) the cart is untouched.
sonnet.q6: Order runs the checkout, driving each step (with its periodic check for stuck orders). The record is Order's DB: each order with its snapshot and status (PENDING, AWAITING_PAYMENT, CONFIRMED, etc.).
sonnet.q7: Provider calls Payment by webhook (signature checked); Payment publishes PaymentSucceeded or PaymentDeclined as an event on the broker, carrying the order id; Order consumes it. If no webhook after 30 min, Payment asks the provider for status and handles it as if a webhook.
sonnet.q8: Payment stores processed webhook event ids and ignores repeats (replies 200, publishes nothing). If a crash caused a duplicate publish, Order acts only on an order in AWAITING_PAYMENT and ignores repeats on finished orders. Claim is also idempotent.
sonnet.q9: Reservation is released: Order sets PAYMENT_FAILED and tells Inventory to release it (marked RELEASED, counts raised), triggered by the PaymentDeclined event (also after the fixed number of failed charge tries). Cart untouched.
sonnet.q10: Order asks Inventory to claim. If the hold lapsed but isn't yet swept, the stock is still set aside and the claim succeeds. If swept, Inventory checks in one transaction that every line's available count covers the order; if so it lowers the counts and the claim succeeds (order fulfilled), otherwise the claim fails and the refund path runs.
sonnet.q11: The refund row is saved first with status PENDING and stays PENDING; it's retried until it succeeds, with an alert after repeated failures (timing undecided). It is tracked in Payment's DB (refunds table). Never dropped.
sonnet.q12: Order publishes OrderConfirmed after the claim succeeds; the Cart service consumes it and empties the cart. If Cart doesn't get it, the broker redelivers; clearing twice is harmless.
